questions.q: All the following are significant demerits or operational risks associated with **computerized accounting systems** EXCEPT
options: High initial capital cost for hardware, software licensing, and personnel training
Risk of massive data loss or corruption resulting from hardware failure, malware, or cyber attacks
Vulnerability to operational downtime during power outages or system maintenance
Inability to process large volumes of routine transactions with high speed and precision
questions.explain:
The ability to process large volumes of routine transactions at very high speed and with consistent mathematical precision is a major **merit (advantage)** of computerized accounting systems, not a demerit. 

High installation costs, power dependence, training requirements, and cybersecurity threats are real demerits.

questions.q: An accounts clerk accidentally enters an invoice amount of ₦50,000 as ₦500,000 into an accounting software package. The software immediately processes and posts the inflated figure throughout the ledgers without error flags. This scenario illustrates which limitation of computerized accounting systems?
questions.explain: The **Garbage-In, Garbage-Out (GIGO)** concept emphasizes that computers process whatever data is supplied to them without subjective judgment. If inaccurate, faulty, or inflated data is entered into the system (Garbage In), the resulting ledger balances and financial reports will also be inaccurate and misleading (Garbage Out).
